prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Conservative Party’s 2010 manifesto is an invitation to rebuild Britain by replacing Big Government with the Big Society: a shift from state control to social responsibility, from centralised power to people power. Rooted in responsibility (fiscal, personal and social), enterprise and aspiration, it declares that we are all in this together—citizens, communities, businesses and government—mobilised to restore trust, prosperity and fairness.

Economic renewal
- End Labour’s debt-driven model with an emergency budget, an Office for Budget Responsibility, £6bn immediate waste cuts, and a credible plan to eliminate most of the structural deficit within a Parliament.
- Stop Labour’s “jobs tax” rise in National Insurance; cut and simplify corporation tax; reduce red tape; back SMEs with procurement access and start-up incentives.
- Rebalance the economy toward saving, investment, hi‑tech and exports; strengthen R&D and STEM; expand apprenticeships; refocus skills funding.
- Safer banking: bank levy; restore prudential supervision to the Bank of England; curb risky trading; boost competition and SME credit.
- Modern infrastructure and regional growth: high-speed rail, superfast broadband without a phone tax, planning reform; expand private-sector jobs outside London.
- Controlled, skills-focused immigration with a non‑EU cap; tighten student visas.

Public services and the Big Society
- Shift power to people and professionals; publish spending and outcomes; foster co‑ops and mutuals; create a Big Society Bank; train community organisers; launch National Citizen Service.
- NHS: increase funding annually; put patients in charge with real choice and transparent results; empower GPs to commission; cut bureaucracy; 24/7 urgent care; Cancer Drugs Fund.
- Education: raise standards with teacher quality, stronger discipline, phonics, rigorous exams; expand academies/free schools; pupil premium; technical academies; protect special schools.
- Families: make Britain the most family‑friendly country; recognise marriage and civil partnerships in the tax system; end the couple penalty; expand flexible working and parental leave; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 more health visitors; protect childhood from commercialisation.
- Welfare and work: a single Work Programme with payment‑by‑results; reassess Incapacity Benefit; require work for the dole for long‑term claimants; make work pay.

Crime, policing and liberty
- Put the system on the side of victims: tougher knife sentencing; cut police paperwork; elected police commissioners; monthly local crime data; dedicated Border Police Force; honest sentencing and rehabilitation paid by results; tackle alcohol‑fuelled disorder and early antisocial behaviour.
- Restore civil liberties: scrap ID cards and databases; a UK Bill of Rights; sensible DNA retention; reform libel laws.

Greener growth and environment
- Lead a low‑carbon economy: Green Investment Bank, a carbon floor, a household Green Deal; smart grid and meters; promote nuclear (no subsidy), CCS, offshore wind and marine energy; secure energy supplies.
- Protect nature: strengthen habitat and species protection; reform CAP/CFP; improve animal welfare; curb bTB with science‑led badger control; honest food labelling; supermarket ombudsman; zero‑waste drive and recycling rewards.

Politics and the Union
- Clean up Westminster: recall for MPs, cut MPs and ministers’ pay, transparency by default, curb quangos, empower Select Committees; localism with neighbourhood planning, referendums, elected mayors.
- National security: National Security Council; back the Armed Forces, renew Trident, fix procurement, restore the Military Covenant.
- Foreign policy: liberal Conservative—principled and practical; strong NATO and US ties; deepen global alliances; support human rights.
- Europe: positive but guarded—no more powers to the EU without a referendum; never join the Euro; seek repatriation of key powers.
- International development: meet 0.7% aid by 2013, with transparency, results, malaria funding, and a focus on trade, property rights and wealth creation.

Sound money, backing enterprise, trusting people: together we can mend the economy, society and politics.
